question.problem: Given that ${\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-4$ and ${\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x=7$ then what is ${\int }_{2}^{8}(5f(x)+4)\,\text{d}x?$
question.worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in the known information into the above gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4)+7={\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 3={\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute the desired integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{8}(5f(x)+4)\,\text{d}x & =5{\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x+4{\int }_{2}^{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(3)+4\cdot x\,{|}_{2}^{8} \\  & =15+4(8-2) \\  & =39.\end{aligned}
$$
